title: 278. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Comparing Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Inverse Relationship Between Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Identify the symmetry relationship between \(y=b^x\) and \(y=\log_b x\).
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the graphs of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\)?

options.label: B
options.text: They are symmetric about the line \(y=x\).

questions.explanation: The functions \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\) are inverses of each other. The graph of an inverse function is obtained by reflecting the original graph across the line \(y=x\). Therefore the two graphs are symmetric about the line \(y=x\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Recall how the graph of an inverse function is related to the original graph.

questions.concept: Domain and Range of a Logarithmic Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain and range of \(y=\log_2 x\).
questions.question: What are the domain and range of \(y=\log_2 x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y=\log_2 x\), the argument \(x\) must be positive, so the domain is \(x>0\). As \(x\) ranges over positive values, the logarithmic output takes every real value, so the range is all real numbers. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Ask which inputs are allowed inside a logarithm, and whether a logarithm can produce negative outputs.

questions.concept: Intercepts of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Compare the intercepts of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\).
questions.question: Which statement about intercepts is correct for \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y=2^x\), when \(x=0\), \(y=1\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,1)\). For \(y=\log_2 x\), when \(y=0\), \(x=1\), so the \(x\)-intercept is \((1,0)\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Substitute \(x=0\) for the exponential graph and \(y=0\) for the logarithmic graph.

questions.concept: Asymptotes of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Compare the asymptotes of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\).
questions.question: Which statement about asymptotes is correct for \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: \(y=2^x\) has horizontal asymptote \(y=0\), and \(y=\log_2 x\) has vertical asymptote \(x=0\).

options.label: B
options.text: \(y=2^x\) has vertical asymptote \(x=0\), and \(y=\log_2 x\) has horizontal asymptote \(y=0\).

questions.explanation: As \(x\to -\infty\), \(2^x\to0\), so \(y=2^x\) has horizontal asymptote \(y=0\). As \(x\to 0^{+}\), \(\log_2 x\to -\infty\), so \(y=\log_2 x\) has vertical asymptote \(x=0\). Therefore option A is correct.

questions.concept: Monotonicity of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs with Base Less Than \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Determine the monotonic behavior of \(y=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x\) and \(y=\log_{\frac{1}{2}} x\).
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes \(y=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x\) and \(y=\log_{\frac{1}{2}} x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(0<b<1\), the exponential function \(y=b^x\) is decreasing, and the logarithmic function \(y=\log_b x\) is also decreasing. Since \(b=\frac{1}{2}\) satisfies \(0<b<1\), both functions are decreasing. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: For each function, decide whether the base is greater than \(1\) or between \(0\) and \(1\), and recall what that means for the direction of the graph.

questions.concept: Inverse Points on Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Identify the corresponding inverse point on \(y=\log_2 x\).
questions.question: If the point \((a,b)\) lies on the graph of \(y=2^x\), which point must lie on the graph of \(y=\log_2 x\)?
questions.explanation: The functions \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\) are inverses. For inverse functions, if \((a,b)\) lies on the first graph, then \((b,a)\) lies on the second graph. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Inverse functions interchange the coordinates of every point.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the inverse of a logarithmic function \(y=\log_b x\).
questions.question: Which function is the inverse of \(y=\log_5 x\)?
questions.explanation: To find the inverse, interchange \(x\) and \(y\): \(x=\log_5 y\). By the definition of logarithm, this means \(y=5^x\). Check: \(\log_5(5^x)=x\), so the two functions undo each other. The function \(y=x^5\) is a power function, not an exponential function, so it does not undo \(\log_5 x\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Interchange \(x\) and \(y\), then rewrite the logarithmic equation in exponential form.

questions.concept: Range Comparison of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Compare the ranges of \(y=3^x\) and \(y=\log_3 x\).
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the ranges of \(y=3^x\) and \(y=\log_3 x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: The range of \(y=3^x\) is \(y>0\), and the range of \(y=\log_3 x\) is all real numbers.

options.label: B
options.text: The range of \(y=3^x\) is all real numbers, and the range of \(y=\log_3 x\) is \(y>0\).

questions.explanation: For \(y=3^x\), the output is always positive, so the range is \(y>0\). For \(y=\log_3 x\), the output can be any real number, so the range is all real numbers. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Ask whether \(3^x\) can ever be negative or zero, and whether \(\log_3 x\) can be negative.

questions.concept: Growth Rate Comparison of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Compare the growth rates of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\) for large \(x\).
questions.question: For \(x>1\), which function eventually grows faster as \(x\) becomes very large?
questions.explanation: For large \(x\), the exponential function \(y=2^x\) increases extremely rapidly, while the logarithmic function \(y=\log_2 x\) increases very slowly. Therefore \(y=2^x\) grows faster, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare how quickly exponential and logarithmic outputs increase for very large inputs.

questions.concept: Limiting Behavior of Exponential and Logarithmic Graphs
questions.learningObjective: Describe the limiting behavior of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\).
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the limiting behavior of \(y=2^x\) and \(y=\log_2 x\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y=2^x\), as \(x\to -\infty\), the value approaches \(0\) but remains positive. For \(y=\log_2 x\), as \(x\to 0^{+}\), the value decreases without bound, so \(\log_2 x\to -\infty\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Consider the horizontal asymptote of the exponential graph and the vertical asymptote of the logarithmic graph.
